title: Tempo capture — Applied ML research log (quant, evals, onboarding) May 09 2028
content:
Tempo capture: short, raw weekly research log — intended for quick handoffs and triage.

Date: 2028-05-09
Attendees: Maya, Jamal, Liang, Priya, Tomás (async notes added)
Meeting length: 40m sync + async updates
Context: rapid push to onboard two compact variants (rwd-v3-mini-q4 and rwd-v3-micro-q4) into Dedicated pool B for latency-sensitive customers. Focus areas: quantization regressions on long-form QA, KV-cache interactions at 4-bit, and microbatch evals to refine batching heuristics.

Pulse / Highlights
- Hit: rwd-v3-mini-q4 shows 1.8x throughput improvement on p50 token generation vs baseline fp16 with ~7% delta in answer F1 on our long-form QA probe (details below).
- Concern: intermittent hallucination spikes in threaded generation when KV-cache warm-starts across conversation turns. Repro steps added.
- Action: short canary rollout to 10% traffic with automatic fallback to rwd-v3-mini-fp16 on quality regression >=6% over baseline.

Experiments run this week (quick summaries)
1) 4-bit symmetric (int4) + KV-prefetch stress test
   - Setup: rwd-v3-mini-q4 with kv-cache prefetch enabled, sequence lengths 512–2048, microbatch sizes [1,2,4].
   - Observations: p95 latency increases when multiple concurrent streams trigger prefetch across different segment boundaries. Root cause hypothesis: cache warming causes extra memcpy stalls in our current prefetch implementation.
   - Metrics: throughput up 1.7–2.0x depending on batch; p95 up by 150–300ms under high concurrency.
   - Next step: PR #214 applies a backoff to prefetch requests; await CI and internal perf run.

2) Eval: long-form QA probe (10k Q/A pairs, curated prompt deck)
   - Models compared: baseline fp16, q4 (rwd-v3-mini), q4 + kl-clip postprocess.
   - Key metrics: Exact-match (EM), F1 (token overlap), answer-rate (non-empty), and perplexity on held-out context.
   - Results snapshot: EM: fp16 62.1% vs q4 57.8% (drop 4.3pt), F1: fp16 78.4 vs q4 72.9 (drop 5.5pt). Perplexity increased ~6% on average for q4.
   - Quick triage: most deltas tied to numeric reasoning and long-coherent-entity recall. Hypothesis: quantization noise accumulates across recurrency in attention layers, especially for tokens encoding long-span anchors.

3) Microbatch scheduling sweep (latency vs cost tradeoff)
   - Goal: find microbatch target that keeps p95 < 400ms for interactive tests while maximizing batching efficiency.
   - Candidate configs: batch_timeout_ms {8, 16, 32}, target_microbatch {1..8}
   - Outcome: For interactive 99% small requests (avg len 48 tokens), batch_timeout_ms=12 + target_microbatch=3 gives best sweet spot in Dedicated pool B. We'll push suggestion into Optimize recommendations.

Onboarding notes for rwd-v3-micro-q4
- Checklist status:
  - Model artifact verified (sha256 ok): YES
  - Compilation profile run on A100-L48: OK (kernel fallback observed on rotary-attn layer under seq_len>1024)
  - Quantization docs updated: draft -> needs SME signoff (Priya)
  - Eval deck integrated into CI: partial (long-form tests still queued)
- Risks called out: rotatory-attn fallback may increase latency significantly on long sequences; recommend gating with fallback policy to fp16 when seq_len>1536 for first pass.

Known issues / triage items
- KV-cache corruption observed in 2 production reproductions: traced to race in cache eviction path when cross-request prefetch + concurrent eviction happen. Ticket ML-5178 opened; hotfix candidate in-thread (Jamal).
- Regression monitor: canary job flagged 3% increase in hallucination rate (measured by hallucination-detector-v2) at 10% traffic. Root-cause hints: beam search length-normalization interaction with q4 logits scaling.
- Perf anomaly: unexpected p95 spike on node pool with mixed q4/fp16 serving due to memory oversubscription when q4 uses 4-bit packing but causes alignment padding increases. Need infra run to re-evaluate packing strategy (Liang).

Decisions / proposals
- Canary rollout policy: 10% traffic, 24h auto-eval window, rollback if F1 drop >=5pt OR hallucination rate +3% over baseline. (Tentative — agree in thread)
- KV-cache prefetch change: enable conservative backoff + serialized eviction path for prefetch-inflight. Jamal to ship patch; schedule infra canary.
- Eval prioritization: prioritize long-form QA and numeric-reasoning probes for q4 onboarding; lower priority for short-chatty benchmarks.

Action items (owner — due)
- Jamal: ship serialized-eviction hotfix branch + run internal perf harness (due 2028-05-12)
- Priya: complete SME review of quantization docs and add mitigation notes for numeric-reasoning failure modes (due 2028-05-11)
- Liang: run packing+memory microbench on Dedicated pool B (A100-L48 & RTX-HG); capture p95/p99 across mix workloads (due 2028-05-13)
- Maya: prepare canary dashboard for rwd-v3-mini-q4 (includes hallucination-detector-v2, EM/F1 probes) and link to rollout policy (due 2028-05-10)
- Tomás: queue extended long-form eval job (10k -> 50k samples) with diverse numeric cases; expected runtime 36h (kickoff 2028-05-10)

Open questions
- Should we adopt an adaptive per-request quantization scaling (per-layer) for long-form contexts to reduce numeric drift? (Priya & Jamal to prototype)
- Can we accept cost delta from forcing fp16 for seq_len>1536 for certain customers in exchange for quality stability? (Product + Solutions to weigh)

Quick notes / scratchpad (raw)
- Observed specific failure case: "invoice #..." style prompts lose consistent entity formatting after ~6 back-and-forth turns on q4; likely floating truncation on token embedding accumulators.
- Slack thread: #applied-ml-quant (pinned message: perf-run-05-08) has some perf traces (see linked_artifacts).
- PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache/pull/214 (prefetch backoff), github.com/redwood-inference/model-tools/pull/332 (quant docs).

Summary / recommended next steps
- Short term: ship eviction serialization & prefetch backoff, run 48h canary at 10% traffic with auto-eval hooks.
- Mid term: instrument per-layer quant noise to inform targeted retraining or kl-clip style postprocessing for numeric-heavy tokens.
- Longer term: consider model-specific serving profiles (i.e., treat rwd-v3-mini-q4 as a different tier with clear quality-latency tradeoffs surfaced to customers).

If you're skimming: key things to watch this week -> ML-5178 (eviction bug), PR#214 (prefetch backoff), canary dashboard (Maya)

End of tempo capture. Please add any missing quick observations inline — this doc is a working capture, not a final writeup.
